transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-07
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE); Diego Ramos (Redwood SE); Priya Narayan (MaplePay Head of Procurement); Liam O'Connor (Security Architect); Hannah Liu (Legal Counsel)
---
Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough): Discussed DPA redlines, KMS options (BYOK/BYOH?), escrow/reserved pricing tiers, and timeline for procurement. Redwood to share SOC2 link and pricing spreadsheet.
---
00:00 Speaker 1 (Alyssa): Hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate the time. Quick intros, we'll keep to the agenda: DPA redlines, KMS, pricing/escrow, and SSO. Diego is our solution engineer and will jump into technical bits.
00:22 Priya: Hi all, thanks. We moved this into our procurement queue; Hannah and Liam are here to cover legal and security. Target to complete vendor selection by end of August, hoping to lock pricing and DPA language.
00:40 Diego: Great, quick question on stack: are you planning to use us for merchant-facing fraud chat features or backend reconciliation? That helps sizing.
01:05 Priya: Primarily fraud and customer support augmentation plus some reconciliation prompts. Volume expectation is approx 200M tokens/month initially. Could spike during holiday windows.
01:28 Liam: On the security side we care about key management (we prefer BYOK), audit logs, and data residency — PCI-scope considerations. We also need to know how Redwood separates ephemeral cache vs persisted logs.
01:48 Hannah: From legal we'll highlight DPA exceptions around sub-processing, data retention, and escrow clauses for long-term availability. We also need indemnity language scoped to certain processed data.
02:10 Alyssa: Understood. High-level: Redwood offers hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem). For BYOK we have KMS integrations and an HSM option for Private. Diego can go into specifics.
02:35 Diego: For BYOK we support customer KMS via standard cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and a bring-your-own-key flow for Dedicated — keys are used to encrypt persistent logs and stored artifacts; live inference still uses ephemeral in-memory buffers, KV cache is not written to disk by default. Note: sometimes transcripts autotexts call it 'K V cash' in our docs, sorry.
03:05 Liam: Good to hear. Do we get audit logs of key access and operator actions? We need to show chain-of-custody to internal auditors.
03:22 Diego: Yes, audit logs are available for Private and Dedicated with retention configurable; hosted has standard logs — we can add an extended retention add-on. Will include sample screenshots.
03:40 Priya: On pricing, procurement needs a 3-year reserved quote for budgeting. Also want an escrow option: if Redwood goes offline what access do we get to model binaries/weights? Is there an escrow fee?
04:02 Alyssa: We can do reserved capacity pricing with an escrow addendum. Typically there's a one-time escrow fee for the archive-and-deposit service plus annual maintenance. We'll send a worksheet with pricing tiers (burst vs baseline throughput).
04:24 Hannah: For the DPA, main asks: restriction on sub-processors, deletion timelines, and audit rights. Also curious about whether Redwood's subcontractors in APAC are used (data residency).
04:45 Diego: We maintain region-specific routing; customers can pin region for data-in-residence, and Private deploys avoid cross-region egress. There may be exceptions for model updates unless you opt for a private model.
05:12 Priya: Timeline check — procurement wants everything by 08/21 to go to legal review. Can we meet that?
05:25 Alyssa: That's tight but doable. We'll prioritize the DPA redline and SOC2 evidence.
---
06:00 (Diego screen share walkthrough, transcript picks up with conflated words)
06:02 Diego: (screen) Here's the config: hosted has flexible throughput, best for fast onboarding; dedicated gives guarantees, predictable latency and reserved capacity; private is air-gapped. Note: we optimize kernels and batching to lower cost, but batching can effect tail latency slightly.
06:35 Liam: Can you quantify 'slightly' — we need 99th percentile latency under 300ms for truncated prompts.
06:48 Diego: For a medium sized 7B-ish model under dedicated reserved nodes we see p99 around 180–260ms at typical seq lengths; hosted depends on load but we can put a hard SLO in contract if needed with a fallback to a smaller model for critical paths. Some of the numbers are in our perf deck — will send.
07:10 Priya: We may consider hybrid: hosted for non-sensitive flows, dedicated for sensitive merchant data. What does billing look like across that?
07:28 Alyssa: Billing can be split — one account with per-route configs, or two accounts depending on legal needs. Reserved pricing reduces per-token by ~40–60% depending on commit. We'll attach an example math sheet.
07:50 Hannah: About escrow: does escrow include model weights or only service config and backups? Need clarity for continuity of service clause.
08:03 Alyssa: Escrow typically includes config, container images, and model artifacts necessary to stand up service; licensing terms for model weights depend on the underlying model license. We'll call out specifics in escrow addendum.
08:30 Priya: Any known competitive caveats? We've talked to BigCloud AI and VaultServe — they offered deeper on-prem support but higher fees.
08:43 Diego: Noted. Our differentiation is the unified runtime and rollout controls; we also provide cost-optimization tooling to reduce unit economics.
---
10:00 (short break in talking, then back)
10:02 Liam: On key rotation: how often are keys rotated and what's the process for emergency key revocation? We need to ensure we can revoke access quickly if a key compromise is suspected.
10:18 Diego: Rotation is customer-controlled for BYOK; revocation will stop new encryptions and we can deprecate any persisted artifacts. We'll provide an ops playbook for revocation and disaster recovery.
10:35 Hannah: Legal would like a sample DPA redline showing our standard exceptions vs Redwood's standard. Any previous customers that refused sub-processor clauses?
10:50 Alyssa: We do sometimes take narrow exceptions for enterprise customers; we'll share precedent language in the redline.
11:10 Priya: Regarding SOC2/ISO, do you provide a SOC2 Type II report and PIAs?
11:24 Alyssa: Yes, SOC2 Type II available upon NDA; we also maintain certain ISO attestations — we'll include certificate scans.
---
15:00 (technical deep-dive snippet)
15:05 Diego: On the KV cache, I want to clarify — for real-time prompting we keep KV in memory, we avoid persisting unless customers enable long-term cache. If long-term cache is enabled it's encrypted with customer's KMS in Dedicated/Private. Hosted defaults to ephemeral, but we can enable encryption at rest with customer key on request.
15:42 Liam: Ok, want to capture that in DPA — ephemeral data is treated differently from retained logs.
16:00 Diego: Yep, we'll add definitions. Also note quantization and model distillation don't change data handling but may affect reproducibility.
---
20:00 (pricing table conversation)
20:05 Alyssa: I'll summarize pricing tiers live: Hosted pay-as-you-go; Dedicated reserved (1yr/3yr) with commitment discounts; Private one-time infra + license. Escrow and extended retention are add-ons. Example: 3-year reserved for your projected volume drops per-token cost by ~55% and includes priority capacity.
20:42 Priya: Need an escrow price example and any thresholds that trigger surcharge (eg cross-region egress).
21:00 Alyssa: We'll include line items for escrow deposit, annual maintenance, and data egress thresholds.
---
25:30 (legal nuance talk)
25:34 Hannah: For indemnity, we want to limit to gross negligence and exclude indirect damages; also want clear data deletion timelines post-termination.
25:50 Alyssa: Our standard includes mutual indemnities and we accept limits with carve-outs for willful misconduct. We'll flag legal exceptions in redline.
26:10 Hannah: Also want to restrict sub-processor list — can you provide the current list and a process to notify future changes?
26:25 Diego: Yes, we'll share the sub-processor register and commit to 30-day notice for material changes, with an opt-out carve.
---
30:00 (procurement milestones)
30:05 Priya: Procurement next steps: need commercial terms, DPA redline and SOC2 evidence to present to the committee on 08/21. Also need sample SLA for p99 latency and uptime commitments.
30:28 Alyssa: We'll aim to deliver the package by 08/10 to give you time. Diego will include the latency spreadsheet.
30:40 Liam: One more thing — how do rollouts and canary deploys work? We need traceability for model updates in case of regressions.
30:55 Diego: Rollouts are baked into the console: canary %, per-route pinning, and automatic fallback to pinned model variants. We maintain rollout audit logs and model version traces.
---
38:00 (questions and minor crosstalk)
38:10 Priya: If we go live in Nov, would reevaluate capacity after the holiday season — can we have a flexible burst cushion?
38:24 Alyssa: Yes, burst buffers available; for Dedicated we can provision burst nodes or allow temporary overage billing.
38:40 Priya: Good. Also double-checking data residency for EU merchant data — we need the EU-only routing option.
38:55 Diego: We have region pinning to EU and will confirm any cross-border service calls that might be necessary for model updates.
---
45:00 (recap and close)
45:05 Alyssa: Recap: 1) Redwood to send DPA redline and SOC2 evidence; 2) Diego to share latency/cost spreadsheet for hosted vs dedicated vs private and show p99 expectations; 3) team to provide escrow pricing and addendum; 4) MaplePay to confirm procurement timeline and legal owners. Target delivery by 2025-08-10.
45:38 Priya: That works, we'll schedule follow-up if needed. Thanks everyone.
45:50 Hannah: Expect a few clarifying legal questions after we review the redline.
46:02 Liam: We'll run a quick internal security check and send any must-have clauses.
46:20 Alyssa: Great — I'll follow up with calendar invite for a handoff call if required.
46:35 (end of meeting)
